name: Hwanung
role: Heavenly prince who descended to rule the earth
fun_fact: Hwanung is said to have come down with three sacred seals and three thousand followers, bringing law and agriculture to the world.

name: Ungnyeo
role: Bear woman who endured the test and became a mother
fun_fact: Her name means 'bear woman', and the mugwort and garlic she ate are still foods associated with spring and healing in Korea.

name: Dangun
fun_fact: Tradition says Dangun ruled for 1,500 years and then became a mountain god at the age of 1,908.

name: Yuhwa
role: Daughter of the river god and mother of Jumong
fun_fact: Yuhwa was later worshipped as Susin, a goddess of caves, alongside her son.

name: Jumong
fun_fact: His name was remembered as a Buyeo word for a skilled archer, and later kings traced their line to him.

name: Bari
role: Abandoned princess who became the first shaman
fun_fact: In many gut rituals, Bari is invoked to guide the soul of the deceased, because she made the journey alone first.

name: Seonyeo
role: Heavenly maiden who marries a mortal woodcutter
fun_fact: The heavenly maidens are often shown descending on a rainbow to bathe in mountain pools, a scene popular in Korean painting.

name: Rabbit
role: Clever rabbit who escapes the Dragon King's court
fun_fact: The rabbit's excuse, that his liver is washed and hanging on a tree, is one of Korean folklore's most quoted jokes.

name: Dragon King
role: Ruler of the sea and its palace
fun_fact: The Dragon King appears in both the rabbit tale and Sim Cheong, but he is not always wise or kind, and the stories often satirise his court.

name: Sim Cheong
role: Filial daughter who returns from the sea as a queen
symbols: the three hundred sacks of rice
fun_fact: Simcheongga is one of the five surviving pansori, and its scene of the blind father regaining sight is a test of a singer's skill.
